title: Leads to Deals Formula
note: Watch one. Try one. Tick one.

modules.title: Before the call
modules.idea: The call is won or lost before you dial.

lessons.title: Welcome to the Leads to Deals Formula
sum: I don't close because I talk well; I close because I show the data, in the right order.
The path: before the call → the call → presentation → objections → closing → follow-up → after the sale.
The rule of this Academy: watch one, try one, tick one.
lessons.do: Write down your current closing rate, so you can see it change.

lessons.title: Read the lead in 2 minutes
sum: Fast and blind loses leads: take 2 minutes before you dial.
Check 5 things: who it is, the words they used (home/family = end-user, ROI/rent = investor, golden visa = AED 2M mark), the source, their time zone, and the budget signal.
Write one lead line before every call. It decides your whole pitch.
lessons.tpl: Lead line: [who] · [end-user / investor / visa] · [source] · [area or project] · [best time to call]
lessons.do: On your next 3 leads, write your one line before you call. Screenshot it. Tick when you have 3.

lessons.title: Run the report before you call, not after
sum: If the client knows a number before you, you've lost the room.
One minute in DealPro: price per sq ft vs the area, upcoming supply, developer and escrow, the exit at handover.
Open with one fact they don't know; send the full report with your name AFTER the call, not before.
lessons.tpl: "This project is [x]% below the area average. I'll show you why."
lessons.do: Before your next call, run one Instant Report and pick your one opening fact.

lessons.title: The 3 questions that decide your pitch
sum: Live in or investment? It changes everything: schools and community, or rent, yield and exit.
Budget including fees: say the 4% DLD first, and listen for cash or mortgage.
When will you decide, and what's making you look now? The 'why now' is what you come back to at 'let me think about it'.
lessons.tpl: 1. Live in or investment?  2. What budget are you comfortable with, including the fees?  3. When would you like to decide, and what's making you look now?
lessons.do: Try these three questions on your next two leads. Write the answers down.

cases: The client who knew more than you

modules.title: Opening the call
modules.idea: 30 seconds to prove you're not the fifth agent calling today.

lessons.title: The first 30 seconds: how to get their attention
sum: Three parts: who you are in one line, why you're calling with one fact, one question that makes them talk.
Use their name, their area and one fact from the report, and give a choice of time.
'I'm busy' or 'just WhatsApp me': always trade the WhatsApp for a time. Never end with 'I'll send details'.
lessons.tpl: "Hi [Name], it's [you]. You asked about [area]. I just ran the numbers: this project is [x]% below the area average, and I wanted to show you why in two minutes. Is now a good time, or shall I call after 6?"
lessons.do: Record your own 30-second opening. Use it on 2 calls.

lessons.title: Find the real budget, timing and motive
sum: Budget: including fees or before? Cash or mortgage? 'If the right one was at 1.7, would you stretch?'
Timing: 'No rush' isn't an answer. Ask: this month or next year, and what would make you decide faster?
Motive: 'What made you start looking now?' Then be quiet, and write their words down.
lessons.tpl: Live or invest · budget [range] incl. fees · cash or mortgage · decide by [date] · motive: [their words]
lessons.do: On your next 2 calls, write the full line.

lessons.title: Book the meeting or video call, not 'I'll send details'
sum: 'Send details' is an ending, not a next step. End with a time.
Summarise in their words, then offer two times, not 'when are you free?'.
Say what you'll send before the call so the video call has a purpose: a decision, not a chat.
lessons.tpl: "I can show you the two best options on video call today after 6, or tomorrow at 11. Which is better for you?"
lessons.do: Use the two-options close on your next 3 calls. Tick when one is booked.

modules.title: The presentation
modules.idea: Present in order and you never lose the room.

lessons.title: The right order: area → supply → developer → project → price → plan → exit
sum: Never start with the project: the client is buying a location.
Go in order every time: area, supply, developer, project, price, plan, exit.
Use the report on screen. Don't read it; point to it.
lessons.tpl: Area → Supply → Developer → Project → Price → Plan → Exit
lessons.do: Present your next project in this exact order. Don't skip supply or developer.

lessons.title: ROI and appreciation without overpromising
sum: Never say 'this will double' or 'guaranteed returns'.
Show real rent for similar units, gross and net yield, then stop.
Show growth as flat / 3% / 5%, conservative first: then they trust the optimistic one.
lessons.tpl: "I can't promise the market. I can show you the data, and you decide."
lessons.do: On your next presentation, show rent, net yield and 3 scenarios. No 'guaranteed'.

lessons.title: Supply: turning 'too many projects' into a reason to buy the right one
sum: Supply isn't your enemy; it's your filter.
Three filters: location inside the area, a developer who finishes on time, price per sq ft below average.
Too much supply means the good ones stand out and the bad ones get stuck.
lessons.tpl: "There are [n] units coming in this area in the next 3 years. That's why we don't buy any project. We buy the right one."
lessons.do: Check the area's supply number in DealPro and write your 3 filters before your next presentation.

lessons.title: Payment plan and cash flow: what they really pay each month
sum: Clients don't buy a price, they buy a monthly payment.
Break it into booking (with the 4% DLD, said first), during construction, and handover.
For investors, show how much of the cost the rent covers, on one page.
lessons.tpl: "Today you pay [amount], including the DLD fee. Nothing hidden. Then [x]% during construction, and [x]% on handover."
lessons.do: Make a one-page payment breakdown for your next client: booking + during + handover + DLD.

lessons.title: The exit: 3 scenarios, and why 'conservative' builds trust
sum: Every presentation ends with the exit: 'If I need to sell, can I?'
Show conservative, realistic and optimistic at handover.
Ask them to buy on the conservative one. If it doesn't work, it's the wrong project, and you say so.
lessons.tpl: "I want you to be happy with the conservative one. If you are, the other two are a bonus."
lessons.do: Present the exit with 3 scenarios on your next deal. Lead with conservative.

modules.title: Objections
modules.idea: Handle objections with data, and never leave one without a time.

lessons.title: 'Let me think about it'
sum: It doesn't mean no; it means 'I need a reason to decide'.
Ask which part: the area, the price or the timing? Then remind them of their own motive.
Offer a small next step with a time, never a vague 'take your time'.
lessons.tpl: "Of course. What part do you want to think about: the area, the price, or the timing?"
lessons.do: Use the 3-step reply (what part + motive + next time) on your next 'let me think about it'.

lessons.title: 'Prices are too high, I'll wait for a correction'
sum: Don't argue. Agree first, then look at the data together.
Show price per sq ft vs the area, and what waiting costs: lost rent, lost payment plan, pricier next launch.
Ask: this project, or the whole market? Then show a cheaper option or the conservative scenario.
lessons.tpl: "I want you to buy because the numbers work even if you're right about a correction."
lessons.do: Prepare your 'cost of waiting' math for your top project: rent lost + price change.

lessons.title: 'I don't trust this developer'
sum: Never defend a developer. Say 'Let's check it together'.
Show facts: delivered projects and on-time record, registration and escrow, construction progress.
If they still don't trust them, suggest another developer. They'll trust YOU more.
lessons.tpl: "That's a fair concern. Let's check it together."
lessons.do: For your top 3 projects, know the developer's delivered projects, escrow and construction %.

lessons.title: 'Another agent offered me a discount'
sum: Don't panic and don't out-discount. Ask which discount and on which unit.
Most 'discounts' are a different unit, floor or view. The developer sets the price.
Offer to compare like for like, and win on data and after-sale service.
lessons.tpl: "Send me what they offered. Same unit, same floor, same view. If it's really better, I'll tell you to take it."
lessons.do: Write your discount reply in your own words and practise it once out loud.

lessons.title: 'My family needs to agree'
sum: It's a buying signal: they like it but can't decide alone.
Ask who else decides and what they care about most.
Send a short video and the report, and book a 15-minute call with the family. Families trust conservative.
lessons.tpl: "Of course. Who else needs to see it, and what do they care about most?"
lessons.do: On your next family objection, ask who, what they care about, and book a call with them.

modules.title: Closing
modules.idea: Close when you hear the signals, and stay with them after they pay.

lessons.title: Signs the client is ready
sum: Five signs: they ask about the process, the unit, the money, they bring the family, they ask about the exit.
Hear two of them? Stop presenting and close.
Keep presenting after they're ready and you talk them out of it.
lessons.tpl: "It sounds like you like this one. Shall we check if that unit is still available?"
lessons.do: On your next 3 calls, write down which buying signals you heard.

lessons.title: The close: EOI, booking and what to say
sum: Confirm the choice: unit, floor, view, price including fees.
Explain the EOI and the next steps simply: booking → SPA → Oqood → escrow.
Ask with two options, send the link while on the call, and stay until it's done.
lessons.tpl: "Shall we do the EOI today so we don't lose that unit, or tomorrow morning? I can send you the link now."
lessons.do: Practise the close out loud once: confirm unit + EOI + next steps + two options.

lessons.title: After the booking: SPA, Oqood and escrow, step by step
sum: Most agents disappear after booking. That's why they never get referrals.
Walk them through the SPA, Oqood and escrow, with proof.
Send the SPA summary, payment schedule and next construction-update date, then update them regularly.
lessons.tpl: After booking: 1) SPA summary  2) Payment schedule  3) Next construction-update date
lessons.do: Create your after-booking checklist and send it to your last client.

modules.title: Follow-up
modules.idea: Follow-up is a system, not luck. Every message has value and a time.

lessons.title: Day 1 / 3 / 7 / 30: what to send each time
sum: Day 1: the report and the agreed time. Day 3: one new fact.
Day 7: proof (a video, a photo, a launch). Day 30: what moved in the area.
Never 'Are you still interested?' Always 'here's what changed, and here's our next time'.
lessons.tpl: "Hi [Name], since we spoke, [one new fact]. The unit you liked is still available. Shall we keep our call on [day]?"
lessons.do: Set Day 1/3/7/30 reminders for your next 3 warm leads.

lessons.title: Use the report again: 'Here's what changed since we met'
sum: The best reason to call a dead lead is what changed, not 'are you ready now?'.
Re-run the report: price per sq ft, units sold, construction, payment plan.
You're the expert who updates them, not the salesman who begs. End with a time.
lessons.tpl: "I just ran the report again. Two things changed. Can I send you the updated one-page report?"
lessons.do: Pick 5 old leads, run updated reports, and send 'here's what changed'.

lessons.title: Revive a dead lead with a new launch or price move
sum: A dead lead didn't buy THAT project at THAT time. Send a new reason.
Three reasons that work: a new launch, a price or plan move, new data (metro, rents, construction).
One message, one reason, one time. No reply? Wait 30 days and try a different reason.
lessons.tpl: "No pressure. Just thought you should see it."
lessons.do: List 10 dead leads, give each one a new reason, and send 5 today.

modules.title: After the sale
modules.idea: One client becomes three: referrals for life.

lessons.title: Updates from booking to handover that make clients feel looked after
sum: Booking to handover is 2–3 years. Disappear and they forget you.
One short update every month or quarter: stage, photo, next payment.
Mark the moments: Oqood done, 50% built, handover near. End with 'Is there anything you need?'
lessons.tpl: "Hi [Name], construction update on your unit: they've finished [stage]. Here's a photo. Your next payment is on [date], [amount]. Any questions, I'm here."
lessons.do: Send a construction update to all your booked clients this week.

lessons.title: The handover moment: asking for the referral the right way
sum: Handover is the happiest moment. Let them enjoy it first.
Remind them how they found you, ask for ONE person, 'even just thinking', no pressure.
Let them choose how to introduce you, and give a small handover gift.
lessons.tpl: "Who do you know who is thinking about Dubai, even just thinking, who I could help with the data, no pressure?"
lessons.do: Write your handover referral script and use it on your next handover.

lessons.title: Yearly portfolio check: resale value and rent
sum: Once a year, a free portfolio check makes you their advisor for life.
Show what it's worth now, what it rents for now, and what to do next.
Hold, rent or sell: advise on their goal, don't push.
lessons.tpl: "It's been a year since you bought. I ran your portfolio check. Can I send you 2 minutes on video?"
lessons.do: Do a portfolio check for 3 past clients this month.

lessons.title: Turning one client into 3: family, friends and colleagues
sum: Family after handover, friends after a portfolio check, colleagues after you help them rent or resell.
Make it easy: 'Just forward them this one-page report with my number.'
Ask for one, not ten. That's how 200 clients become 600.
lessons.tpl: "Just forward them this one-page report with my number. I'll look after them like I looked after you."
lessons.do: Ask one past client for one introduction this week.

modules.title: Sam's story
modules.idea: From 1 in 10 to 3 in 10 presentations: what changed when I started using data.

lessons.title: How I closed 3 out of every 10 presentations
sum: I used to talk a lot, send brochures and close maybe 1 in 10.
One client knew the price per sq ft and I didn't. That night: never again.
Report before every call, data in order, the 3 questions: my closing rate tripled. Don't learn more scripts; learn the data.
lessons.do: Write down your closing rate out of your last 10 presentations. Check it again in 30 days.
